stages.label: Birth–5
stages.title: Early age
stages.detail: Pregnancy, newborn and early childhood support.

stages.title: Working age
stages.detail: Labour-market, livelihood and social insurance protection.

stages.label: 65–death
stages.title: Old age
stages.detail: Elderly income security, pension, care and disability inclusion.

stages.label: Death→birth
stages.title: Cycle reset
stages.detail: A small transition wedge showing death, renewal and birth.

policies.name: Family Card
policies.lead: Ministry of Social Welfare / DSS
benefits: Tk 2,500 monthly cash support for poor and vulnerable households
FY2026–27 target: 41 lakh households; card generally issued in the female head’s or mother’s name
Household-level entry point for lifecycle, livelihood and shock-response services
policies.note: Shown as a full lifecycle ring because it protects households rather than one narrow age group.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 public budget allocation: Tk 14,500 crore.

policies.name: Women and girls lifecycle protection
policies.group: Women and girls across the life cycle
policies.lead: MoWCA with MoSW, MoLE and local government
benefits: Female household member as primary Family Card recipient
Girls’ education, safe learning environment and dropout prevention
Maternity, childcare, vulnerable women and widow-related protection
policies.note: This is the women-focused whole-circle layer requested by the user.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: Disability Allowance and Education Stipend Programme
policies.group: Persons with disabilities at all ages
policies.lead: Ministry of Social Welfare / DSS
benefits: Allowance: Tk 1,000 monthly
Education stipends: Tk 1,000 primary, Tk 1,100 secondary, Tk 1,200 higher secondary and Tk 1,400 higher level
FY2026–27 target: 39 lakh beneficiaries
policies.note: Disability is cross-cutting and therefore spans the full lifecycle.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 public budget allocation: Tk 4,715.45 crore.

policies.name: Mother and Child Benefit Programme
policies.lead: Ministry of Women and Children Affairs
benefits: Tk 850 monthly cash support; paid quarterly
FY2026–27 target: 18.95 lakh beneficiaries
Nutrition, antenatal/postnatal care and behaviour-change linkages
policies.note: Official FY2026–27 programme figures; shown in the early-childhood wedge.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 public budget allocation: Tk 1,968.20 crore.

policies.name: Early childhood care linkages
policies.lead: Health, local government and social welfare services
benefits: Birth registration and referral to health and nutrition services
Parenting, early learning and childcare linkages
Protection of children without adequate family care
policies.note: A service layer supporting the MCBP rather than a single cash scheme.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: Primary School Stipend
policies.lead: Ministry of Primary and Mass Education
benefits: Support for school enrolment and attendance
Universal coverage for students in government primary schools
Complements school meals in poor and food-insecure areas
policies.note: Age range is indicative for primary-school age.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: Harmonized Secondary/Higher Stipend
policies.lead: Ministry of Education
benefits: Supports attendance and completion
Priority for poor households, girls, children with disabilities and hard-to-reach areas
Can include fee waivers and dropout prevention measures
policies.note: Age range is indicative; actual education eligibility may vary.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: School Meal Programme
policies.lead: Ministry of Primary and Mass Education
benefits: Nutrition support through school meals
Initial focus on poverty-prone and food-insecure areas
Supports attendance, learning readiness and food security
policies.note: Shown as an early school-age layer.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: Employment Generation Programme for the Poorest (EGPP)
policies.lead: Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief
benefits: Daily wage: Tk 500; Tk 550 for a Sardar
Two annual work cycles of 40 days each; weekly payment
FY2026–27 target: 3.70 lakh beneficiaries
policies.note: Official EGPP figures are used; this is tax-financed workfare, not unemployment insurance.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 EGPP public budget allocation: Tk 1,632.84 crore.

policies.name: Unemployed Workers’ Protection Programme
policies.lead: Ministry of Labour and Employment
benefits: Non-contributory support distinct from unemployment insurance
Temporary assistance for unemployed workers
Can bridge workers not yet covered by contributory NSIS
policies.note: This is assistance, not a contributory insurance branch.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: National Social Insurance Scheme (NSIS)
policies.lead: MoLE Social Security Unit / future authority
benefits: Integrated protection for employment injury, maternity, sickness and unemployment
Branch-wise funds, contributions, claims administration and grievance redress
Designed to begin in formal sector and expand administratively
policies.note: NSIS is not yet fully rolled out; no approved aggregate contribution or benefit amount is loaded.
policies.fundingNote: NSIS is not yet fully rolled out; no verified aggregate FY2026–27 public allocation or approved contribution schedule is loaded.

policies.name: Employment Injury Insurance / EIS
policies.lead: MoLE / future EIS authority
benefits: Pilot covers about 4 million export-oriented RMG workers for permanent disability and survivor pensions
Disability benchmark: at least 60% of former wage × disability degree; survivor benchmark: at least 50% of former wage
Voluntary brand financing: 0.019% of annual RMG export value; no statutory payroll premium yet
policies.note: Operational pilot; monthly pension top-ups depend on age and last wage. No single verified public-budget allocation is loaded.
policies.fundingNote: The pilot is financed through voluntary brand contributions of 0.019% of annual RMG export value; no single verified FY2026–27 public-budget allocation is loaded.

policies.name: Maternity Insurance
policies.lead: MoLE with MoWCA and health services
benefits: Proposed pooled income replacement during maternity-related absence
Current Labour Act benefit is employer-liability, wage-linked and allows up to 120 days
No approved NSIS premium rate or pooled benefit amount
policies.note: Proposed NSIS branch; not yet launched as a pooled national contributory scheme.
policies.fundingNote: No approved national NSIS premium, pooled benefit amount or separate verified FY2026–27 allocation is loaded.

policies.name: Sickness Insurance
policies.group: Workers temporarily unable to work due to illness
policies.lead: MoLE / future NSIS authority
benefits: Proposed cash income replacement during certified temporary incapacity
Waiting periods, medical certification and coordination with sick leave remain to be designed
No approved national contribution rate or cash-benefit amount
policies.note: Identified as an NSIS branch; not yet launched as a national contributory scheme.
policies.fundingNote: No approved national contribution rate, cash-benefit amount or separate verified FY2026–27 allocation is loaded.

policies.name: Unemployment Insurance
policies.lead: MoLE and employment services
benefits: Proposed temporary income replacement for involuntary unemployment
Would require contribution records, job-search conditions, training and placement services
No approved national contribution rate, replacement rate or duration
policies.note: Identified as an NSIS branch; not yet launched. Separate from tax-financed EGPP/workfare.
policies.fundingNote: No approved national contribution rate, benefit schedule or separate verified FY2026–27 allocation is loaded.

policies.name: Vulnerable Women Benefit
policies.lead: Ministry of Women and Children Affairs
benefits: 30 kg rice per month for vulnerable women
FY2026–27 target: 10.40 lakh beneficiaries
Livelihood, skills and economic-inclusion support
policies.note: Working-age women-focused layer.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 public budget allocation: Tk 2,297.70 crore.

policies.name: Widow Allowance
policies.lead: Ministry of Social Welfare / DSS
benefits: Tk 700 monthly cash support; paid quarterly
FY2026–27 target: 30 lakh beneficiaries
For widowed, husband-deserted and distressed women meeting programme criteria
policies.note: Official FY2026–27 programme figures; starts in adulthood and continues into old age.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 public budget allocation: Tk 2,535.12 crore.

policies.name: Universal Pension Scheme
policies.group: Contributors, informal workers, migrants and retirees
policies.lead: National Pension Authority / Ministry of Finance
benefits: Probash monthly contributions: Tk 2,000 / 5,000 / 7,500 / 10,000
Samata: Tk 1,000 monthly, split Tk 500 subscriber + Tk 500 government
policies.note: Operational voluntary contributory pension. The loaded public allocation is only the FY2026–27 Samata Scheme budget, not the total UPS corpus.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 public budget allocation for the National Pension Authority (Samata Scheme): Tk 10 crore. This excludes subscriber contributions and the wider pension corpus.

policies.name: Old Age Allowance
policies.lead: Ministry of Social Welfare / DSS
benefits: Tk 700 monthly cash support; paid quarterly
FY2026–27 target: 62 lakh beneficiaries
Priority for poor, landless and vulnerable older persons
policies.note: Shown from age 65 to death in the visual model.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 public budget allocation: Tk 5,239.25 crore.

policies.name: Pension for Retired Government Employees
policies.lead: Ministry of Finance and relevant public bodies
benefits: Retirement income security for former public servants
Survivor/family pension where applicable
Continues as a separate employment-based pension pillar
policies.note: Shown from indicative retirement age.
policies.fundingNote: FY2026–27 Pension Management public allocation: Tk 35,379.40 crore.

policies.name: Consolidated Humanitarian Assistance
policies.lead: Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief
benefits: Food, cash, shelter and livelihood recovery after disasters
Can scale vertically or horizontally during shocks
Linked to dynamic registry and early-warning triggers
policies.note: Shock risks can affect all ages; therefore it spans the whole circle.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: Consolidated Food Support Programme
policies.lead: Ministry of Food / Ministry of Commerce
benefits: Harmonized food-support instruments
Supports poor households during food-price shocks
Can link with Family Card for better targeting
policies.note: A whole-life covariate risk layer.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: Migrant Worker Protection and Reintegration
policies.lead: MoEWOE, WEWB, BMET and missions abroad
benefits: Pre-departure finance, orientation, contract verification and skills support
Overseas assistance, wage recovery, legal aid and repatriation
Returnee reintegration, entrepreneurship and psychosocial support
policies.note: Working-age ring for migration cycle protection.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: Freedom Fighters and July Martyrs/Injured Support
policies.lead: Relevant line ministries
benefits: Cash assistance and harmonized support for eligible groups
Medical treatment, rehabilitation and education/livelihood support where relevant
Beneficiary verification and unified programme management
policies.note: Special support is not age-specific; shown across the life course.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.

policies.name: Farmer’s Card
policies.lead: Agriculture, fisheries, livestock and finance institutions
benefits: Access to subsidised inputs, concessional credit and crop insurance
Can extend to fish farmers, livestock rearers and agro-entrepreneurs
Links productive support with risk protection
policies.note: Included as a worker/livelihood risk layer from the reform text.
policies.fundingNote: No verified FY2026–27 public allocation is loaded for this policy layer.
